name: C-Reactive Protein
overview: C-Reactive Protein is a health topic that clinicians and patients frequently discuss during care planning in India and worldwide. Key considerations include c-reactive protein (crp) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation; it is an acute-phase protein of hepatic origin that increases following interleukin-6 secretion by macrophages and t cells; its physiological role is to bind to lysophosphatidylcholine expressed on the surface of dead or dying cells in order to activate the complement system via c1q. This summary is educational and should be paired with professional medical evaluation.
purpose: In routine practice, c-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Health professionals note that it is an acute-phase protein of hepatic origin that increases following interleukin-6 secretion by macrophages and T cells.
Health professionals note that its physiological role is to bind to lysophosphatidylcholine expressed on the surface of dead or dying cells in order to activate the complement system via C1q.
